requirements.text: After a successful `authenticate`, `session/new` on the same connection does not fail with `-32000` (authentication required). `capability="inferred:authMethods"` is documentation-only (same encoding as ACP-MODES-001): the test runs only when `authMethods` is non-empty and `--tck-auth-method <id>` names one of its non-terminal entries, and SKIPs otherwise -- the client MUST NOT `authenticate` with a `terminal` method, and the TCK cannot guess a valid `methodId`. An `authenticate` error SKIPs too, since a real agent may legitimately reject bad or expired credentials. When it returns a result, that result is a JSON object (shape only) and the `session/new` check above is the one hard assertion.

Only exercised when `--allow-logout`/`--tck-allow-logout` is given (destructive: may revoke the operator's own credentials); SKIPs otherwise.

requirements.text: If `initialize`'s `authMethods` is empty or absent, `session/new` does not fail with `-32000` (authentication required). `session/new` may fail that way only if the agent requires authentication, and with no advertised method there is no defined remedy. Only `-32000` is judged here; any other `session/new` failure is ACP-SESSION-001's concern. `skip_if_auth_gated` only excuses `-32000` when `authMethods` is non-empty, so with it empty the session-dependent tests fail on their own terms too.

When the client advertises `clientCapabilities.auth.terminal: true`, the `initialize` result validates against the schema, including any `type: "terminal"` auth methods it now advertises (`args` an array of strings, `env` a string map). `type` is the `AuthMethod` discriminator, so a `type: "terminal"` entry is also checked against `AuthMethodTerminal` itself (the schema's `anyOf` would otherwise accept it as an `agent` method). Passes with no terminal-specific evidence if the agent advertises none. The TCK never launches the terminal flow.
After `session/cancel` during an in-flight `session/prompt`, the prompt request resolves with a successful result whose `stopReason` is `cancelled`, not an error.

Content and tool call updates (`user_message_chunk`, `agent_message_chunk`, `agent_thought_chunk`, `tool_call`, `tool_call_update`) for the cancelled session arrive before the `session/prompt` response; none arrive after it. Session-state updates (e.g. `session_info_update`, `usage_update`) are allowed outside a turn and are not judged. "None arrive after it" is checked with a quiet period derived from --tck-timeout (tck.v1.conformance._helpers.quiet_period), not an infinite wait.

The agent MUST NOT call `fs/read_text_file` or `fs/write_text_file` during a session/prompt turn when the client did not advertise `fs` support -- the mock client always advertises `clientCapabilities: {}`, so no `fs/*` request may ever be observed. PASS is vacuous for an agent that never needs file access.

The agent MUST NOT call any `terminal/*` method during a session/prompt turn when the client did not advertise `clientCapabilities.terminal === true`. PASS is vacuous for an agent that never needs a terminal.
The agent MUST NOT call `elicitation/create` during a session/prompt turn when the client did not advertise any elicitation mode. PASS is vacuous for an agent that never elicits.

The agent MUST NOT send a `notice` session update unless the client advertised `clientCapabilities.session.notices` -- checked over a whole connection with `clientCapabilities: {}` (session/new, one prompt turn, `session/load` when advertised, then a quiet period). PASS is vacuous for an agent that never sends notices.

The agent MUST NOT send `compaction_update` or `compaction_summary_chunk` unless the client advertised `clientCapabilities.session.compaction`, live or during `session/load` replay -- checked the same way as ACP-CLIENTCAP-004. PASS is vacuous for an agent that never reports compaction.

The agent MUST NOT send `plan_update` or `plan_removed` unless the client advertised `clientCapabilities.plan` -- checked the same way as ACP-CLIENTCAP-004. Unstable feature: an agent that does not implement plan operations never sends these and passes vacuously.

The agent MUST NOT send `subagent_update`, `session_message`, or `session_message_chunk` unless the client advertised `clientCapabilities.subagents` -- checked the same way as ACP-CLIENTCAP-004. Unstable feature: an agent that does not expose subagents never sends these and passes vacuously.
`session/close` for an existing, idle session succeeds with a schema-valid empty-object result.

`session/close` on a session with an in-flight `session/prompt` cancels the ongoing work as if `session/cancel` had been called, so the prompt resolves with `stopReason: "cancelled"`. Derived obligation, medium confidence -- the spec states the cancel-as-if via X2 and never says "close" explicitly next to `stopReason`; inferred by reference to the cancellation contract (X3).

When `session/new` returns a non-null `configOptions`, every entry's `currentValue` is valid per its declared type: a `boolean` entry's `currentValue` is a bool; a `select` entry's `currentValue` is one of its `options` (flat or grouped shape). Inferred support, same encoding as ACP-MODES-001 -- `capability="inferred:configOptions"` is documentation-only.

`session/set_config_option` responds with a schema-valid result carrying the *complete* list of every previously-advertised `configOptions` id (not only the changed one), with the new value applied to the option that was changed -- stated as a MUST twice in the docs.

An agent MUST NOT include a `type: "boolean"` config option in any `configOptions` payload unless the client advertised `clientCapabilities.session.configOptions.boolean: {}` -- a genuine client- controlled MUST NOT. Checked on `session/new`'s result, a `session/set_config_option` result, `session/load`/`session/resume` results when advertised, and any `config_option_update` seen meanwhile. Passes vacuously if the agent has no config options, or none of `type: "boolean"`, at all.

requirements.text: `session/delete` for a session created earlier on the same connection succeeds with a schema-valid empty-object result. Deleting an active session is implementation-defined, so the session is closed first when `close` is advertised; otherwise an error from deleting the still-active session SKIPs rather than FAILs.

requirements.text: Every error object's `message` is non-empty and free of embedded newlines (the schema says it "should be limited to a concise single sentence" -- checked leniently, exact wording is never asserted); `data` needs no further shape check. Evidence comes from an unrecognized-method request and an invalid-params `session/new`. A probe the agent leaves unanswered contributes no sample (silence on the custom method is ACP-EXT-001's concern); passes vacuously if the agent returns no errors.
A request with invalid params (`session/new` without the required `cwd`) yields error `-32602` (Invalid params). SKIPs on `-32000`, since the agent may check authentication before params.

requirements.text: A request to an unknown, `_`-prefixed custom method receives *some* response -- a result or any error, not necessarily `-32601`. Custom requests must get a response (ACP follows JSON-RPC 2.0, where every request expects a result or error); only the specific `-32601` code is a "should", which is ACP-JSONRPC-004's concern.
An unrecognized `_`-prefixed custom notification is ignored: the connection stays usable and a subsequent `session/new` still succeeds. That it gets no reply is ACP-JSONRPC-003's concern.

Behaviour on a syntactically-valid JSON value that is not a JSON-RPC envelope (`{"foo": "bar"}`) is recorded, same shape as ACP-INFO-PARSE-001. Spec silent; reference SDKs disagree (rust-sdk replies -32600, python-sdk silently drops it). Never asserts on the probed behaviour itself, but still FAILs if the prerequisite `initialize` handshake fails.

requirements.text: Behaviour on a malformed (non-JSON) stdin line is recorded -- reply `-32700` with `id: null`, reply otherwise, or stay silent -- along with whether the connection remains usable afterwards (a subsequent `session/new` still succeeds). Spec silent; reference SDKs disagree (rust-sdk replies -32700, python-sdk silently drops the line). Never asserts on the probed behaviour itself, but still FAILs if the prerequisite `initialize` handshake fails.

requirements.text: The error code (if any) returned for `session/prompt` against a `sessionId` the agent never created is recorded, never asserted -- v1 does not specify one. Even a successful result is only recorded. Never asserts on the probed behaviour itself, but still FAILs if the prerequisite `initialize`/`session/new` handshake fails.
`initialize` succeeds and the result validates against the schema, with an integer `protocolVersion`.
When the client requests protocol version 1, the agent returns 1.

When the client requests an unsupported protocol version (65535), the agent returns a successful result whose integer `protocolVersion` (a) is not 65535 -- echoing an unsupported version verbatim breaks the MUST to answer with the latest supported version -- and (b) is at least the version the same agent returns for a v1 request. Equality is not required: an agent supporting several versions (e.g. 1 for a v1 request, 2 for anything >= 2) may answer higher than its v1 answer. The probe's params also carry a v2-shaped `info` object alongside the v1 fields: dual-version routers, and v1-only Rust SDK agents (which parse `info` for any requested version >= 2), reject such a request without it with `-32602`, a params-shape reason unrelated to version negotiation.
`agentInfo` with `name` and `version` is present in the `initialize` result.
A response's `id` echoes the request `id` exactly, for both integer and string ids.
A response carries exactly one of `result`/`error`; an error object has an integer `code` and a string `message`.

Notifications never receive a response, success or error. Probed with `session/cancel` (no prompt in flight), an unrecognized `_`-prefixed custom notification, and `$/cancel_request` for a request id the agent never saw. Messages the agent itself initiates (they carry `method`) are not responses. Concluding "no response arrived" is a heuristic wait (a quiet period derived from --tck-timeout) -- see tck.v1.conformance._helpers.quiet_period.
An unknown method yields error `-32601`. Only the code is a "should"; replying at all is ACP-EXT-001's concern.
After an erroneous request, the connection remains usable (subsequent requests still succeed).

requirements.text: After a `$/cancel_request` notification naming a request id the agent never received, the connection stays usable: a subsequent `session/new` still succeeds. An agent is free to ignore `$/` notifications it does not support, but a notification must never break the connection.

After `$/cancel_request` for an in-flight `session/prompt`, the agent still sends exactly one response to that request: a schema-valid `PromptResponse` result, or an error with code `-32800` (Request cancelled). Any other error code fails. An agent that does not support `$/cancel_request` and finishes the turn normally also satisfies this. SKIPs ("cancellation not exercised") when the prompt resolved before the notification could be sent, or when no response arrives within --tck-timeout: support is optional, so an ignored notification and a still-running turn look the same.
`session/list` with `params: {}` succeeds with a schema-valid `ListSessionsResponse` whose `sessions` field is present as an array.
`session/list` filtered by a `cwd` that no session uses returns `sessions: []` (an empty array, never `null`, never an error).
`session/load` with a valid `sessionId`, `cwd`, and `mcpServers` succeeds with a schema-valid `LoadSessionResponse` object.

requirements.text: Every history update belonging to the `session/load` replay arrives before the `session/load` response; no history-kind update (`user_message_chunk`, `agent_message_chunk`, `agent_thought_chunk`, `tool_call`, `tool_call_update`) for the session arrives after it. Session-state updates (e.g. `available_commands_update`) are allowed outside a turn and are not judged. No claim is made about how many history updates are replayed or their fidelity.

The `session/load` empty result is `{}` (an object), not `null`. The schema allows only an object and the docs example shows `{}` (corrected from `null` upstream in `d89c8d31`). ADVISORY only: upstream's Rust schema crate tolerates `null` for defaultable payloads on receipt (`ac82df63`, deserialization only; the schema is unchanged), and the Python SDK coerces it too, so mandatory schema validation (ACP-LOAD-001) treats `null` as equivalent for an all-optional object response.
A `session/prompt` carrying `_meta` (including a `traceparent` key, reserved for trace context) is accepted and resolves with a normal, defined `stopReason`.

When `session/new` returns a non-null `modes`, it validates against the schema and `currentModeId` refers to one of `availableModes` (derived from the field descriptions, not a stated MUST). Inferred support, not a boolean/object marker in `initialize` -- there is no `agentCapabilities` field for this; support is inferred from `session/new`'s own response (`capability` is a documentation-only string, not a real initialize-result path -- see module docstring of `test_session_config.py`). SKIPs with reason 'session/new returned no modes/configOptions' when absent.

`session/set_mode` to a different `modeId` succeeds with a schema-valid `SetSessionModeResponse`. No echo notification is required (§7: "do not assert an echo notification"), but if a `current_mode_update` (`session/update` with `sessionUpdate: "current_mode_update"`) for the session is observed, it MUST carry the schema field name `currentModeId` -- the docs' example at `session-modes.mdx:117-119` showed `modeId` until upstream fixed that docs bug in `b96b439`; the schema was always the source of truth here.

requirements.text: A text-only `session/prompt` resolves with a successful result whose `stopReason` is one of the defined `StopReason` values.

Every `session/update` notification emitted during a prompt turn validates against the schema and carries the `sessionId` of the session being prompted. An agent that emits no updates during the turn is allowed (Req 1 places no MUST on emitting them, only on being *able* to send them); this test passes vacuously in that case.

requirements.text: A prompt containing a `resource_link` content block alongside text resolves with a successful result whose `stopReason` is a defined value. `initialization.mdx:247` and the schema's `PromptCapabilities` description both make Text and ResourceLink the baseline every agent MUST support; `content.mdx:31` only mentions text but does not exclude `resource_link`, which carries no prompt-capability requirement.

Every file path the agent emits is absolute: `locations[].path` and `diff` content `path` on any `tool_call`/`tool_call_update`, and `sessions[].cwd` in a `session/list` result (when `list` is advertised). Absolute means POSIX `/...`, a Windows drive path, or a UNC path. Passes vacuously when the agent emits no paths.

When `agentCapabilities.promptCapabilities.image` is `true`, a `session/prompt` containing an `image` content block (`ImageContent`: `data`, `mimeType`) alongside text resolves with a successful result whose `stopReason` is a defined value.

requirements.text: Every message the agent emits during a basic exchange validates against the vendored v1 schema.

No agent-emitted spec object (a request/notification `params`, a successful response `result`, or an error object) carries a root-level key outside its `$def`'s resolved `properties` union (following `allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf`/`$ref`). `_meta` is allowed, except on error objects: `Error` defines only `code`, `message` and `data`. Implementations MUST NOT add custom root fields; ADVISORY only because the check is an approximation -- the vendored schema has no `additionalProperties: false`, so the allowed-keys union is built by hand (`tck.v1.validation.find_unknown_root_keys`), and a false positive against a conforming agent would be an unfair FAIL.
`session/new` with an absolute `cwd` and `mcpServers: []` succeeds with a non-empty string `sessionId`, and the response validates against the schema.

requirements.text: Two `session/new` calls on the same connection return distinct `sessionId`s.

`session/new` with one stdio MCP server entry (`name`, absolute `command`, `args`, `env`) succeeds with a schema-valid result -- all agents MUST support the stdio MCP transport. The entry points at a stub MCP server shipped with the TCK (`tck.v1.conformance._mcp_stub`), run by the TCK's own Python interpreter.

After `session/new` with that stdio MCP server entry and one prompt turn, the agent has launched the stub server and sent it an MCP `initialize` request. SHOULD-level ("Agents SHOULD connect to all MCP servers specified by the Client"); the prompt turn gives an agent that connects lazily a chance to do so before the check.

After the client closes stdin, the agent process exits on its own within the close grace period, without needing SIGTERM/SIGKILL. Informational: the spec defines no shutdown method or timing, only that the client closes stdin and terminates the subprocess. FAILs if the agent needed a signal, or if `initialize`/`session/new` got no response at all (timeout or exit).

The byte count of stderr output observed during an ordinary exchange is reported for information only, never asserted (the agent MAY log UTF-8 to stderr). FAILs only if `initialize` or `session/new` got no response at all (timeout or exit).

`session/new` with `systemPrompt: {mode: "append", content: [<text block>]}` succeeds with a schema-valid result: every agent advertising the capability supports `append`, and MUST accept text content blocks. Unstable feature.
